patch.value: Adopt --respect-item-release in changelog scripts and close the shipped-but-stale Block Kit truncation tracker

Adopts pm-changelog 2026.7.24 --respect-item-release across the changelog scripts and bumps the devDependency, then uses the new capability to close pm-slack-gx2h, whose fix shipped in v2026.06.07 but whose tracker stayed open because closing it would have retro-dated the work into the current release window.
all four changelog scripts pass --respect-item-release; pm-changelog devDependency is ^2026.7.24; pm-slack-gx2h is closed and appears under the 2026.6.7 heading not Unreleased; changelog:check green

value.author: claude
value.text: Verified with the published pm-changelog 2026.7.24: pm-slack-gx2h attributes to the 2026.6.7 heading and changelog:check exits 0. Underlying fix independently re-verified before closing — 60/60 unit tests assert the 3000/150 limits against oversized inputs, and a live 6000-char notify produced a 149-char ellipsised header with 0 limit violations across 14 blocks in the notify and digest payloads.

value.author: claude
value.text: Greptile review finding adopted: the daily release workflow invokes pm-changelog DIRECTLY (npx pm-changelog, three times) rather than through the npm scripts, so patching only package.json left the generation path that actually produces the published CHANGELOG.md and RELEASE_NOTES.md without the flag while release:check validated with it. Added --respect-item-release to all three release.yml invocations so generation and validation agree. YAML re-validated.
